text: Machine learning is a way for computers to learn from data without being explicitly programmed. In supervised learning, we give the computer a set of training data that includes both inputs and their correct outputs. For example, we might show it pictures of animals and label each one as “cat” or “dog.” Using this data, the computer builds a model, which is essentially a set of rules or patterns it discovers. Once the model is ready, it can make predictions on new, unseen data. To judge its quality, we measure the accuracy, which tells us how often the model’s predictions are correct. Better training data usually leads to a more accurate model.
